<STRUCT_0001>
The analogue of this chapter for algebraic spaces is the chapter entitled
``Bootstrap'', see
Bootstrap, Section <REF_0001>.
That chapter already contains some representability results.
Moreover, some of the preliminary material treated there we already
have worked out in the chapter on algebraic stacks.
Here is a list:
<STRUCT_0002>
<STRUCT_0003> We discuss morphisms of presheaves representable by algebraic spaces in
Bootstrap, Section
<REF_0002>.
In
Algebraic Stacks, Section
<REF_0003>
we discuss the notion of a <MATH_0001>-morphism of categories fibred in groupoids
being representable by algebraic spaces.
<STRUCT_0004> We discuss properties of morphisms of presheaves representable by
algebraic spaces in
Bootstrap, Section
<REF_0004>.
In
Algebraic Stacks, Section
<REF_0005>
we discuss properties of <MATH_0002>-morphisms of categories fibred in groupoids
representable by algebraic spaces.
<STRUCT_0005> We proved that if <MATH_0003> is a sheaf whose diagonal is representable
by algebraic spaces and which has an <ACCENT_0001>tale covering by an algebraic
space, then <MATH_0004> is an algebraic space, see
Bootstrap, Theorem <REF_0006>.
(This is a weak version of the result in the next item on the list.)
<STRUCT_0006>
<LOCKED_0001>
We proved that if <MATH_0005> is a sheaf and if there exists an algebraic
space <MATH_0006> and a morphism <MATH_0007> which is representable by algebraic
spaces, surjective, flat, and locally of finite presentation, then
<MATH_0008> is an algebraic space, see
Bootstrap, Theorem <REF_0007>.
<STRUCT_0007> We have also proved the ``smooth'' analogue of
(<REF_0008>) for algebraic
stacks: If <MATH_0009> is a stack in groupoids over
<MATH_0010> and if there exists a stack in groupoids
<MATH_0011> over <MATH_0012> which is representable
by an algebraic space and a <MATH_0013>-morphism <MATH_0014>
which is representable by algebraic spaces, surjective, and smooth
then <MATH_0015> is an algebraic stack, see
Algebraic Stacks, Lemma
<REF_0009>.
<STRUCT_0008>
Our first task now is to prove the analogue of
(<REF_0010>) for algebraic
stacks in general; it is
Theorem <REF_0011>.
